extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers and experimentalists (early-modern scientists) seeking methods for investigating and manipulating natural bodies
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for classifying kinds of natural motion and for designing experiments and practical methods to investigate, control, and make useful transformations of natural bodies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibit species / simple elements of motions
rubrics_metrics.description: Set out the species, or simple elements, of motions, tendencies, and active powers which are most universal in nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a classification useful for investigation (not merely abstract); accept that divisions may be changed, reduced, or added to as better natural orders emerge; classifications should terminate in matter and construction to be practically useful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion of transmission or of passage
rubrics_metrics.description: The power by which the actions of bodies are impeded or advanced by the medium, varying with the nature of the bodies and of the medium (e.g., different media for light, sound, heat, magnetic action).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When investigating phenomena, consider whether the medium transmits or modifies effects and account for medium-specific adaptations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Royal or political motion
rubrics_metrics.description: A motion where a predominant/governing part of a body checks, subdues, reduces, and regulates the other parts, forcing them into order (seen strongly in animal spirits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine predominance of parts in whole bodies (e.g., spirits regulating blood/urine); consider how removing or emitting the governing element allows decomposition or transformation; use this concept in 'wrestling instances' of predominance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spontaneous motion of revolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Bodies with tendency to move and placed favorably pursue themselves (revolve) or rest; favourable placement leads to circular/eternal motion, unfavourable to rest, others move straight to unite with congenial bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat revolution as a distinct species of motion and analyze its concrete differences (see separate dimensions) and whether it belongs to heavens or descends to air/water.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference of revolution: centre about which bodies move
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether and what centre a body revolves about is a dimension of revolution to be determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and specify the centre of revolution in experiments or observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference of revolution: poles round which they move
rubrics_metrics.description: The poles (axes) about which bodies revolve form a distinct difference to be recorded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe existence, position, and possible mobility of poles in rotational motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference of revolution: circumference/orbit distance from centre
rubrics_metrics.description: The relative distance of the orbit/circumference from the centre is a distinguishing feature of revolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure and report orbital radii and how they vary among bodies or conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference of revolution: velocity (speed of revolution)
rubrics_metrics.description: The greater or less speed with which bodies revolve is a key dimension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantify relative velocities and relate them to causes or resisting forces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference of revolution: direction of motion
rubrics_metrics.description: The direction (e.g., east to west or the reverse) is an aspect of revolution to note.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record directionality explicitly when studying celestial or terrestrial rotations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference of revolution: deviation from perfect circle (spiral relative to centre)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deviation from a perfect circle by spiral lines at greater or less distance from the centre is a distinguishable variation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between circular and spiraling trajectories and measure spiral parameters relative to centre.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference of revolution: deviation from circle (spiral relative to poles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deviation from a circle by spiral lines at varying distances from the poles is another distinct variation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe and record spiral deviations with respect to the poles/axes as distinct from centre-based spirals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference of revolution: spacing of spirals
rubrics_metrics.description: The greater or less distance of these spirals from each other is a separate difference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure spacing between successive turns when spiraling motion occurs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference of revolution: variation of movable poles
rubrics_metrics.description: Variation of the poles (if movable) affects revolution, especially when circular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate pole mobility and its effect on rotational behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion of trepidation
rubrics_metrics.description: A motion of constant trembling/restlessness when bodies are placed in an intermediate state (neither entirely proper nor improper) — e.g., heart/pulse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider trepidation where bodies are in mean states; record continuous small oscillations and their causes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion of repose / abhorrence of motion
rubrics_metrics.description: A tendency of dense bodies to stand by their own weight and to resist motion; bodies seek to recover former state when moved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine how dense bodies oppose motion and attempt to return to rest; use this to explain behavior under disturbance and partial representations due to spirits in substances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect wrestling instances to show predominance of powers
rubrics_metrics.description: Find examples ('wrestling instances') where different motions/powers predominate or yield to show in what manner and proportion they predominate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gather experimental cases (e.g., magnets lifting sixty times their weight, levers, breaking points of materials, flow through chinks, effect of gunpowder vs sulphur alone) to exhibit relative strength and yielding thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine how yielding occurs: cessation vs constrained exertion
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine if yielding motions are annihilated by predominance or continue as constrained, possibly invisible efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design experiments and thought-experiments (bound man struggling; musket-ball projected up vs down) to test whether the suppressed motion still exerts effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect rules of predominance
rubrics_metrics.description: Derive general rules governing which motions prevail, e.g., more general desired advantage corresponds to stronger motion; connection may be more powerful than gravity; small private goods don't defeat public ones except in small quantities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From wrestling instances abstract rules about generality, scope, strength, and contexts of predominance; use these rules to predict outcomes in new cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerogative instances: suggesting instances
rubrics_metrics.description: Select instances which suggest or point out what is advantageous to mankind; science should aim to make judicious inquiries and wishes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the store of knowledge, emphasize examples that are practically useful and that can guide applications to practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerogative instances: generally useful instances
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances that are broadly applicable and recurrent, saving labor and avoiding needless repetition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect generally useful examples (tools, contrivances) and apply them across arts; document methods that recur across cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method 1 — Exclusion of all that impedes and disturbs
rubrics_metrics.description: Act upon natural bodies by excluding elements that impede (e.g., common air, rays of heavenly bodies) to preserve or control substances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use hermetic closing, lutum sapientiæ, oil films, powders, wax, pitch, immersion in quicksilver, subterranean storage (grottoes), or submerged vessels to keep off air/sun; ensure quantity preservation; experiment with techniques like inverted tubs for divers and preservation methods for wine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method 2 — Compression, extension, agitation, and similar violence
rubrics_metrics.description: Use mechanical violence (compression, extension, agitation) to induce locomotion, destroy organic qualities, or alter position-related properties like color or taste.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test whether such violent changes can produce permanent transformations (e.g., condensing air to water) by perseverance and aids (harmonies); try sealing experiments, condensed water tests, flattened/glass egg experiments, and observe whether changes persist or are transient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method 3 — Heat and cold
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ heat and cold as principal engines to produce transformations; observe that man has abundant means for heat but limited means for cold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diligently collect instances of different kinds and degrees of heat (sun rays, lightning, flame, furnaces, moist/dry heats, animal heat) and cold (frost, caverns, snow/ice burial, immersion in rivers or quicksilver); investigate gentle and periodic heating/regulating intervals as well as substitutes for cold and their effects on condensation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate species and degrees of heat
rubrics_metrics.description: Systematically classify and examine every species and degree of heat and its peculiar effects (direct/reflected/refracted rays, lightning, flame, furnace types, moist heats, dry heats, animal heat).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare violent vs gentle heats; study effects of gradual approach/retreat and periodicity of heat (important for generation and delicate conformations); avoid assuming equable heat suffices for processes that require inequality and periodic change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitutes and methods for cold and condensation
rubrics_metrics.description: Since natural cold is scarce, search for substitutes or methods that effect condensation (the operation of cold).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider burial in cold places, immersion, use of certain substances (astringents, soporifics) in animals, and other means. Classify condensations into four kinds: (1) simple compression; (2) contraction after escape of finer parts; (3) cohesion of homogeneous parts formerly mixed with others; (4) harmony (latent condensing powers). Investigate each experimentally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condensation by simple compression
rubrics_metrics.description: Condensation effected by violent compression, which is limited by elasticity and may be transient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test permanence by prolonged perseverance and supports; consider combinations with other methods if simple compression alone fails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condensation by contraction after escape of finer parts
rubrics_metrics.description: Condensation produced when coarser parts remain and finer parts escape (as in induration by fire).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate heating/extinguishing cycles and processes where volatile parts leave and coarser parts harden and contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condensation by cohesion of homogeneous parts
rubrics_metrics.description: Condensation occurring when homogenous parts return from a dispersed state into a denser, cohesive form (e.g., sublimated mercury returning to a smaller volume).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explore purification and reaggregation processes in metals and other materials to obtain denser states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condensation by harmony (application of condensing substances)
rubrics_metrics.description: Condensation achieved by application of substances that condense by some latent power (harmonies), more common in animal medicines than in inanimate bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search for and test such harmonies cautiously; investigate alleged natural examples (e.g., plants dripping dew) as potentially important leads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method 4 — Continuance (detention / application of time)
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow a body to remain undisturbed and protected for a measurable time so internal motions operate (continuance yields delicate effects unlike fire).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate continuance in open vs hermetically sealed vessels (open: separations; sealed: mixtures; partly closed admitting air: putrefaction); gather instances (wine aging, slow incorporations) and record temporal dependencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method 5 — Checking or directing motion (direction of motion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrest, repel, allow, or guide a body's motion by shape and position (vessels, strainers, internal bodies) to favor desired outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use vessel shapes (upright/reversed cones), curves, alternating constrictions/dilations, strainers, internal bodies (pebbles, egg white) to direct motion in casting, modelling, refining syrups, etc.; document form-function relations carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method 6 — Peculiar harmonies, sympathies and antipathies
rubrics_metrics.description: Occult specific properties (sympathies/antipathies) that cause certain bodies to correspond or repel; these are obscure but include broad correspondences (e.g., sulphur, mercury quaternions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First determine forms and conformations before seeking subtle harmonies; investigate large-scale correspondences (sulphur/oil/flame vs mercury/water/air) and relations between bodies and their supporting menstruums (soil, climate); apply to grafting and cultivation experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method 7 — Seasonable and proper alternation, series, and succession
rubrics_metrics.description: Use timely alternation and proper sequencing of methods (compression, heat, time, direction, harmony) to achieve transformations more effectively than by single violent action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan experiments with ordered application and alternation of methods (periodicity, intervals) as many natural processes depend on regulated inequality and sequence rather than continuous uniform application.
